name: Craft degree rituals (Entered Apprentice / Fellow Craft / Master Mason)
stated_reason: Preserving the experience of initiation; traditional obligation
description: The three ceremonies through which a candidate becomes a Master Mason including obligations and lectures.
notes: Wording differs widely by jurisdiction and era.

name: Modes of recognition (signs / grips / passwords)
stated_reason: Mutual recognition among members
description: Gestures and words used by members to identify each other by degree.

name: Grade initiation rituals (Neophyte 0=0 to Adeptus Minor 5=6)
stated_reason: Protecting candidates and the efficacy of the ritual
description: Ceremonial initiations for the Outer and Inner Order grades.

name: Knowledge lectures and inner-order teachings
stated_reason: Teaching must follow the candidate's progress
description: Instructional papers on Kabbalah / astrology / geomancy / ritual magic issued grade by grade.

name: Degree rituals and higher-degree sexual magic teachings
stated_reason: Danger of misuse by the unprepared
description: Initiation rituals of the degree system and the instructions reserved for the highest degrees.

name: OT III materials
restricted_to: Members who completed the preceding levels
stated_reason: Claimed harm to those who learn it unprepared
description: Upper-level course materials containing a cosmological narrative (widely reported as the Xenu story).

name: Temple endowment ceremony
stated_reason: The ordinances are sacred and are not discussed outside a temple (CLM-0042)
description: Temple ceremony including covenants / signs and tokens.
notes: Penalty gestures were removed from the ceremony in 1990.

name: Kitāb al-Ḥikma (Epistles of Wisdom)
stated_reason: Sacred knowledge reserved for the initiated
description: The core scriptural corpus of the Druze faith.

name: Initiation puja and personal mantra
stated_reason: Effectiveness depends on correct personal instruction
description: A Sanskrit ceremony performed at instruction and a mantra given privately to each student.

name: Elders' manual (Shepherd the Flock of God)
stated_reason: Guidance intended for appointed elders
description: Internal handbook covering congregational procedures including judicial committees.

name: Highest yoga tantra empowerments and samaya commitments
restricted_to: Disciples who have received the empowerment from a qualified teacher
stated_reason: Practice without empowerment and a qualified teacher is held to be ineffective or harmful; samaya binds the disciple to secrecy
description: Initiation ceremonies (abhiṣeka) that authorise a disciple to practise a particular tantric deity system, together with the vows that go with them and the tantras and commentaries those practices rely on.
notes: Some empowerments, such as Kālacakra, are given by the Dalai Lama to very large public audiences.

name: Kanjō (abhiṣeka) and the mantra and mudrā transmissions
restricted_to: Disciples consecrated by a Shingon master; full transmission only to those receiving the master's consecration (denbō kanjō)
stated_reason: Esoteric teaching can only be received through direct transmission from master to disciple
description: Consecration rites that admit a disciple to esoteric practice, and the mantras, hand gestures and visualisations taught under them.

name: Śrīvidyā mantra and initiation (dīkṣā)
stated_reason: The mantra is regarded as the goddess herself and is held to be effective only when received from a guru
description: The fifteen- or sixteen-syllable mantra of the goddess Lalitā Tripurasundarī and the initiations through which it is given.

name: Kaula ritual of the five elements (pañcatattva)
restricted_to: Initiates gathered in a ritual circle (cakra)
stated_reason: The rite is held to be dangerous for, or misunderstood by, the uninitiated
description: A rite using five substances or acts conventionally forbidden in orthodox practice, interpreted literally or symbolically depending on the lineage.

name: Upanishads and Vedāntic instruction restricted by eligibility (adhikāra)
restricted_to: Twice-born (dvija) males studying with a teacher
stated_reason: Only those qualified by birth and initiation are entitled to study the Veda
description: The Upanishads, regarded as part of the Veda, and the teaching of their meaning, which classical Advaita reserved to qualified students.
notes: Restrictions by caste and gender have been widely relaxed since the 19th century.

name: Initiation (bayʿa) and silent remembrance (dhikr khafī)
restricted_to: Disciples initiated by a shaykh of the order
stated_reason: Litanies and methods are held to be effective only when passed down the chain of masters (silsila)
description: The pledge by which a disciple enters the order, and the silent remembrance and related exercises the shaykh then teaches.

name: Initiation (ikrar) and the ayin-i cem ceremony
stated_reason: Keeping the order's secret (sır) is a duty of the initiate
description: The ceremony by which a candidate is admitted to the order, and the communal rite held among initiates.

name: Maʿaseh Merkavah and Maʿaseh Bereshit
restricted_to: A single qualified student at a time
stated_reason: Speculation on these subjects is dangerous for the unprepared
description: Esoteric teaching on Ezekiel's vision of the divine chariot and on the account of creation, which early rabbinic law allowed to be taught only under strict conditions.
notes: Kabbalistic texts have been printed since the 16th century.

name: Rites of the Mysteries
stated_reason: The rites of Demeter and Kore were not to be spoken of
description: What was done, said and shown to initiates in the sanctuary at Eleusis.
notes: Profaning the Mysteries was a criminal offence at Athens.

name: Seven-grade initiation system
stated_reason: Not recorded: no Mithraic text explaining the cult survives
description: A sequence of grades through which initiates advanced, known mainly from inscriptions and images in Mithraic temples.

name: Powamu ceremony and Katsina society initiation
restricted_to: Initiated members of the Katsina and Powamu societies
stated_reason: Ceremonial knowledge belongs to the societies and clans responsible for it and may not be shared outside them
description: A winter ceremony in which children are initiated into the Katsina society.
notes: Hopi villages have restricted outsiders' access to many ceremonies and banned photography and recording.

name: Women's restricted knowledge concerning Kumarangk (Hindmarsh Island)
restricted_to: Ngarrindjeri women with the relevant authority
stated_reason: Restricted women's knowledge that may not be disclosed to men or outsiders
description: Knowledge asserted in 1994 by a group of Ngarrindjeri women opposing a bridge to Hindmarsh Island, given to the federal minister's reporter in sealed envelopes marked for women only.
notes: Its authenticity was the subject of a Royal Commission and later litigation. The content has not been published.

name: Palladian rite (alleged Luciferian high degrees)
restricted_to: Alleged: selected high-degree Masons and women initiates
stated_reason: None recorded: the rite is attested only in hoax literature
description: A Luciferian rite said by the literature of the Taxil hoax (1892–1897) to stand above all Masonic rites and to be directed from Charleston.
notes: Kept as a record of a fabrication. Léo Taxil publicly admitted in April 1897 that the material was invented (CLM-0044).

name: Initiation ceremony and the thirty-six articles of the oath
stated_reason: Not recorded beyond the oath itself, which requires secrecy even within the family (CLM-0045)
description: The ceremony by which new members are admitted to the lodge, including the reading of the oath and the blood rite.

name: Recognition signs, passwords and tea-cup signals
stated_reason: Mutual recognition among members
description: Verses, answers and arrangements of tea-cups by which members recognise each other at home, on the road and on board ship.

name: Alchemical and meditative methods and their oral instructions (koujue) transmitted under covenant
restricted_to: Disciples judged worthy, who make a covenant with the master
stated_reason: Given to the unworthy, the methods do not work and master and disciple both suffer misfortune (CLM-0050)
description: Scriptures of elixir alchemy and of meditation on the One, and the oral instructions that went with them, handed on only by covenant with pledges.

name: Initiation and the doctrine of the Meaning, the Name and the Gate
stated_reason: Not yet recorded from an Alawite source
description: The staged initiation of young men into the religion and the teaching they then receive about 'Ali, Muhammad and Salman al-Farisi.

name: The Sāvitrī (Gāyatrī) verse and Vedic recitation, conferred at initiation (upanayana)
restricted_to: Twice-born (dvija) males initiated by a teacher; the uninitiated and Śūdras excluded
stated_reason: Sacred learning is a treasure to be kept from scorners and given only to the pure and attentive; taking the Veda without permission is theft (CLM-0058)
description: At initiation a boy of the three higher classes receives the Sāvitrī verse from his teacher, which opens Vedic study to him; those not initiated in time lose the right to it, and the uninitiated may not recite Vedic texts.

name: Secret transmissions (hihō) and the shōkanjō consecration of the mountain retreats
restricted_to: Shugenja (yamabushi) who complete the mountain retreats (nyūbu)
stated_reason: Not yet recorded from a Shugendō source
description: Secret lore and consecrations given at the end of a period of ascetic practice in the mountains, through which the practitioner is identified with Fudō Myōō.

name: Church Handbook of Instructions, Book 1 (Stake Presidencies and Bishoprics)
stated_reason: Prepared only for use within the church by its local leaders
description: The leaders' manual of church administration, including procedures for church discipline, issued to local leaders and not sold or published.
notes: Replaced in 2020 by an openly published General Handbook (CLM-0077).

name: Men's restricted ceremonies, sites and designs recorded by C. P. Mountford
stated_reason: Knowledge given in confidence and not to be seen by women, children or uninitiated men
description: Knowledge of sacred sites and objects, paintings and rock engravings explained to Mountford in confidence during fieldwork in 1940, which he recorded and photographed and printed in Nomads of the Australian Desert (1976).

name: Men's secret-sacred ceremonies, songs and tjurunga in the Strehlow Collection
restricted_to: Initiated men of the relevant estates and their authorised custodians
stated_reason: Ceremonial knowledge belongs to its custodians and is restricted by gender and initiation
description: Ceremonies, song verses, films, sound recordings and sacred objects recorded or collected by T. G. H. Strehlow from about 1932 to the 1970s.
notes: Much of the song material was published by Strehlow in Songs of Central Australia (1971).

name: Karmamudrā: sexual practice with a consort
restricted_to: Advanced tantric practitioners and their consorts
stated_reason: Highest yoga tantra practices are bound by samaya and disclosed only to qualified initiates
description: Use of an actual sexual partner (as distinct from a visualised one) in the completion stage of highest yoga tantra, including by lamas who were publicly monks.

name: Skull ritual (dokuro honzon) attributed to the Tachikawa lineage
description: A medieval Japanese esoteric rite in which a human skull is consecrated, built up with layers of sexual fluids and lacquer, and kept for years until it is believed to speak.
notes: Known mainly from the polemic Juhō yōjin shū by the monk Shinjō (c. 1270). Whether it belonged to the Tachikawa lineage is disputed.

name: Degree initiations and the 'shooting' of the migis shell
restricted_to: Initiated Mide' of the corresponding degree
stated_reason: Secrets and remedies that have been paid for lose their virtue if passed on for nothing (CLM-0080)
description: The ceremonies of the four degrees, in which officiating priests 'shoot' the sacred migis shell into the candidate with their medicine bags, and the songs, remedies and instruction given at each degree.

name: Hamatsa initiation and the eating of flesh
restricted_to: Initiated members of the hamatsa society and the other winter-ceremonial societies
stated_reason: Not yet recorded from a Kwakwaka'wakw source
description: The initiation of a new hamatsa, who is held to be taken away to the woods by the cannibal spirit BaxbakualanuXsiwae and returns possessed, biting people and eating human flesh before he is tamed.
notes: Boas (SRC-0076, pp. 440–441) already reports that by the 1890s the biting was done by a sleight of hand (CLM-0082).

name: The noaidi drum (goavddis) and the meaning of its figures
stated_reason: Not yet recorded from a Sámi source
description: The drum painted with figures of gods, spirits, people and animals, struck to move a pointer across the figures for divination, healing and finding lost things, and the knowledge of what each figure means.
notes: Nearly all early knowledge of the figures comes from missionaries and court records (CLM-0086).

name: The mushroom vigil (velada) and the 'saint children'
restricted_to: Mazatec families and patients gathered by a healer; kept from outsiders until 1955
stated_reason: Outsiders who take the mushrooms without need spoil them: they lose their purity and force (CLM-0094)
description: An all-night rite in which a healer and the participants eat psilocybin mushrooms in the dark, and the healer chants and consults the mushrooms about sickness, lost things and absent people.
notes: Made public by R. Gordon Wasson's account in Life (1957) of a vigil led by María Sabina, whom he called Eva Mendez.
